clue.text: Fail to keep it up as a maligned therapist

blocks.note: first meaning: to contract or wilt, here the bawdy sense of losing an erection
second meaning: the disparaging slang for a psychiatrist

explanation.surface: A sneer at a therapist who cannot perform, in typical Private Eye smut.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye clues are often rude on purpose; the first half is about impotence, the second about head doctors.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to contract or wither, and the noun is short for headshrinker, slang for a psychiatrist.

clue.text: Nervous sort of brainy networkers

blocks.note: surface reading: clever people who work a room making contacts, a little anxious
setter's reading: junctions in the nervous system that link brain cells into networks

explanation.surface: A description of anxious, clever people schmoozing at a networking event.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the gaps between nerve cells across which signals pass, joining neurons into the brain's networks.

clue.text: see 10ac.
Unlike Thatcher's "No" to the French press?

definitions.text: Unlike Thatcher's "No" to the French press?

blocks.note: NON is French for no
to iron clothes is to press them

explanation.surface: Margaret Thatcher famously said no, no, no to Europe; here she refuses the French newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: Thatcher was the Iron Lady, so anything unlike her is not iron; the whole clue also reads as a fabric that says no to pressing.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric described this way needs no pressing after washing, and anything unlike the Iron Lady is likewise not of iron.

clue.text: How to annoy a luvvie: lift leg

blocks.note: to lift something is to put it up
a leg of a journey or race is a stage

explanation.surface: Advice on irritating a pompous actor: raise a leg, perhaps to trip or kick them.
explanation.walkthrough: A luvvie is British slang for a gushing, self-regarding actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealing the limelight from a fellow performer on stage is the surest way to irritate a vain theatrical type.

clue.text: Cameron crushes independent oil development around Conservative London area

indicators.note: to crush something is to squeeze it tight, so the prime minister grips the next piece inside
a development changes how something is arranged, so these letters are reordered
the reworked letters go round the party abbreviation that follows

blocks.note: David Cameron was Prime Minister in 2015
I is the standard abbreviation for independent
taken as written, to be reshuffled
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister stamps on an independent oil project somewhere near Tory territory in London.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers in a row: the first piece is built and complete before the reworked letters wrap round the party abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a district of central London in Westminster, lying between Victoria station and the Thames.

clue.text: Makes contact between members?

blocks.note: surface reading: getting in touch with fellow members of a club or party
setter's reading: members as body parts, so the contact is a grope

explanation.surface: Someone keeping in touch with fellow party or club members.
explanation.walkthrough: Members can be limbs or genitals, so the innocent networking becomes groping, typical Private Eye innuendo.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to fondle someone indecently, and also to make small cosmetic improvements to something.

clue.text: Craft of King George entertaining idle bastard

indicators.note: a bastard version of something is corrupted or debased, so these letters are messed up
to entertain is to take in a guest, so the king's letters hold the next piece

blocks.note: GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George
taken as written, to be reshuffled

explanation.surface: A monarch's vessel is used to host some lazy good-for-nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: An engineless aircraft that rides air currents is a type of craft, the word covering vessels of air and sea.

clue.text: (& 24dn.) Maybe stony David puts round into Labour worthless sort

blocks.note: labour is work
a round shape is the letter O
a fart is slang for a contemptible, useless person

explanation.surface: A stony-faced politician called David turns a worthless sort into Labour.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests David Cameron or Miliband; the real David is Michelangelo's marble statue.
explanation.definitionFit: Michelangelo's David is a famous marble sculpture, a stone example of a celebrated artistic creation.

clue.text: Liberal undone, having first accepted sly suggestion

indicators.note: liberal means free and loose, so these letters are freely rearranged

blocks.note: something accepted is in, as in fashion or favour
taken as written, to be reshuffled

explanation.surface: A Liberal Democrat brought down by an insinuation, as several were in 2015.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal' looks like the party but is the anagram signal; 'having first' puts IN at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: An indirect hint, usually suggestive or disparaging, is an insinuation, a sly remark rather than a plain statement.

clue.text: (& 2dn.) Nigel and two Ukip leaders going mad with room for foreign cabaret

indicators.note: leaders are those at the front, so only the opening letter is taken, here twice over
going mad means losing order, so all these letters are scrambled together

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter of Ukip, counted twice
taken as written

explanation.surface: Nigel Farage and party leaders run riot, perhaps over making room for foreigners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Room for foreign' reads as immigration politics, but room is fodder and the definition is the last two words.
explanation.definitionFit: The Moulin Rouge is the famous Parisian cabaret venue of can-can fame, a nightclub abroad from a British view.

clue.text: Show up a Speaker's Lords member?

indicators.note: a speaker's version is what is heard when spoken, so we go by sound and not spelling

blocks.note: a peer is a member of the House of Lords

explanation.surface: A query about whether to embarrass a member of the House of Lords, with the Commons Speaker nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speaker' suggests the Speaker of the Commons, but it only means something said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: To show up and to arrive or come into view are the same idea, so the verbs are straightforward synonyms.

clue.text: Dubbed King Miliband after dark?

indicators.note: after places the Labour leader's name behind the word for darkness

blocks.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
night is the dark part of the day
Ed Miliband led Labour into the 2015 election

explanation.surface: Mocking Ed Miliband, crowned king of Labour only in the dark, or nicknamed King Miliband.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch makes someone a knight by touching each shoulder with a sword, the ceremony called dubbing.

clue.text: Many followed the 2015 Election, seeing Labour's end and Nige's breaking with nameless countries

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, which alone is kept
something breaking falls apart, so these letters are rearranged
nameless means without a name, and the abbreviation for name is dropped

blocks.note: the final letter of Labour
taken as written, to be reshuffled
countries are nations

explanation.surface: After the 2015 election, Labour is finished and Nigel Farage breaks from the European nations.
explanation.walkthrough: N is the abbreviation for name, so nameless countries is NATIONS without its N. Nige is Nigel Farage.
explanation.definitionFit: Miliband, Clegg and Farage all quit as party leaders after the 2015 general election, so many departures from office followed it.

clue.text: Hospital visitor's pain aggravated by small measure in jug

indicators.note: something aggravated is stirred up and disturbed, so these letters are jumbled
in places the small measure inside the word for jug

blocks.note: taken as written, to be reshuffled
jug and tit are both slang for a woman's breast
an en is a small printer's measure of width

explanation.surface: A hospital caller's discomfort is made worse by a small drink in a jug.
explanation.walkthrough: Jug is not a pitcher but slang for a breast, typical Private Eye vulgarity; the small measure sits just before its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone admitted to stay in hospital overnight is a resident patient there, a visitor for a while in a loose sense.

clue.text: (& 22dn.) Conservative Right abandoned humour and heart for a start – don't take seriously

indicators.note: something abandoned is left behind, so the letter for right drops out
a start is the beginning, so only the opening letter is taken

blocks.note: a Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party
R is the abbreviation for right
wit is humour
the first letter of heart

explanation.surface: The Tory right has lost its sense of humour and its heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heart' wants to mean the middle letters, but 'for a start' takes its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To trifle with a thing, treating it lightly or playfully, is to refuse to give it serious attention.

clue.text: Right low-spirited like the party faithful

blocks.note: right and true both mean correct
feeling blue is feeling low

explanation.surface: Right-wingers are glum, the way loyal party members often are.
explanation.walkthrough: Blue is the Conservative colour, so the phrase means staunchly loyal, especially to the Tories.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes unwavering loyalty, especially to the Conservative Party whose colour is blue, as with committed activists.

clue.text: Could be Labour's got shit on Brenda? Sun: "Killjoys!"

blocks.note: Labour is an example of a political party
poop is excrement
Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for the Queen, Elizabeth Regina
S is the abbreviation for Sunday or sun

explanation.surface: A Sun front page shouting about Labour having dirt on the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye calls Queen Elizabeth Brenda; ER stands for Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: These are people who spoil others' fun at a celebration, gloomy spoilsports who dampen everyone's enjoyment.

clue.text: Nick to cause a bit of a car crash?

definitions.text: cause a bit of a car crash

blocks.note: to nick a criminal is to arrest them, or run them in
taken as written

explanation.surface: Asking whether stealing a car leads to a crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' looks like stealing a car, but it is British slang for arrest.
explanation.definitionFit: To collide with another vehicle or object is to hit it, a minor bump in traffic.

clue.text: Natural penis with electronic component?

blocks.note: the penis is the male sexual organ
IC is an integrated circuit, an electronic component

explanation.surface: A smutty query about a man fitted with a battery-powered part.
explanation.definitionFit: Food grown without artificial chemicals is described this way, meaning produced by unforced, untreated processes.

clue.text: Drink, um, is a depressant

blocks.note: to down a drink is to swallow it in one
um and er are both sounds of hesitation

explanation.surface: A hesitant warning that alcohol brings you down.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedative drug, or anything dispiriting, is informally called this because it lowers mood and activity.

clue.text: Indecisive voter's refrain: "Ukip's second today"

indicators.note: second points to the letter in position two of the party name

blocks.note: to refrain is to hold back, as in the command don't
the second letter of Ukip
today means at the present time

explanation.surface: A floating voter keeps repeating that Ukip is in second place today.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refrain' looks like a chorus, but it is the verb, giving the command form.
explanation.definitionFit: Pollsters label undecided respondents with this phrase, the answer they give when asked how they will vote.

clue.text: see 15dn.
Left crushed by cabinet minister's mitts

indicators.note: something crushed by another is squeezed inside it, held within the minister's name

blocks.note: Michael Gove was a Conservative cabinet minister
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: The political left is flattened by a Tory minister's hands.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Gove was Justice Secretary after the 2015 election.
explanation.definitionFit: Mitts is informal for hands, and also for coverings worn on them, so it is a synonym for handwear.

clue.text: see 8dn.
Provoked, Sun gets even – not very well hidden

indicators.note: not means without, so the abbreviation for very is taken away
provoked means stirred up, so these letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written, to be reshuffled
taken as written
V is the abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: The Sun newspaper, provoked, takes its revenge but makes a poor job of hiding it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not very well hidden' reads as a single phrase, but 'not very' removes V and 'well hidden' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something completely concealed cannot be seen by anyone, so it remains out of sight altogether.

clue.text: Appendage cover with fancy lace

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate and decorated, so these letters are reworked into a new pattern

blocks.note: a tent is a covering shelter
taken as written, to be reshuffled

explanation.surface: A dress accessory: a covering trimmed with ornate lace.
explanation.definitionFit: An octopus's long flexible arm is a limb-like extension of its body, an attached outgrowth.

clue.text: Love quota delivered by speechifier

definitions.note: a phrase describing what the speaker gives, standing for the noun

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
a ration is a fixed allowance or quota

explanation.surface: A long-winded orator hands out portions of love.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal public address, the kind of grand speech a pompous speaker gives, is this noun.

clue.text: A quarter Scottish, they recklessly make cuts

indicators.note: a quarter of an eight-letter word is its opening two letters
acting recklessly means acting wildly and without order, so these letters are scrambled

blocks.note: the first two of the eight letters of Scottish
taken as written, to be reshuffled

explanation.surface: Part-Scottish politicians are slashing budgets carelessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuts' sounds like austerity, but the definition is mowing with a long curved blade.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to mow grass or crops with a long curved blade, sweeping strokes that slice through stems.
